reasoning_traces.think:
The MCBLT framework addresses multi-camera tracking by integrating 2D detection with 3D spatial reasoning. It begins with multi-view image aggregation into a bird’s-eye view (BEV) representation, leveraging camera calibration to project 2D observations into 3D space. This enables robust object localization and reduces ambiguity from viewpoint differences. Subsequently, hierarchical graph neural networks (GNNs) associate 3D detections across time and space, modeling object trajectories as nodes in a dynamic graph. The spatio-temporal transformer layer enhances this by enabling long-range temporal dependencies and global spatial awareness. These components form a dual system: one that reasons about object identity through ReID and another that reasons about motion through GNNs. Failure modes include misalignment in camera calibration, occlusion-induced feature loss, and breakdown in temporal consistency. The framework's strength lies in its modular design, allowing each component to be optimized independently while maintaining end-to-end performance.
